clue.text: Place providing virtual exchange?

parts.note: an online venue where people swap messages rather than goods: the exchange is of words, and the place exists only on the internet

explanation.surface: Somewhere a virtual trade or stock exchange might be housed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange' suggests trading or a stock market; here it is an exchange of conversation, held online.
explanation.definitionFit: An internet site for live typed conversation is a virtual meeting place where remarks are exchanged.

clue.text: Popular and low man in church strangely empty

indicators.note: in means the man word goes inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the word strangely is removed, keeping first and last letters

explanation.surface: A man in church behaves oddly vacant and base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' looks like an adverb for 'empty'; here 'empty' acts on the word strangely, keeping only its outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cheesy is crowd-pleasing yet cheap and tacky, both popular and of low quality.

clue.text: Name entering property for approval

indicators.note: entering means the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: an asset is an item of property

explanation.surface: A name is added to a property deed to get it approved.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving assent means giving agreement or consent, a formal approval.

clue.text: Member of group's entourage I adore abroad

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hanger-on of a pop group gushes about life overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' rearranges I and ADORE. 'Group' is a band, whose touring crew carries the gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the crew who sets up equipment for touring musicians is part of a band's travelling team.

clue.text: Revised role to change without second old actor

indicators.note: to change means the letters are put into a different order
without means the letter for second is taken out of the word next to it

explanation.surface: A part is rewritten, minus a second, for a veteran performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without second' takes S from REVISED, leaving REVIED; 'to change' rearranges REVIED and ROLE. The actor (1938-1999) starred in Oliver! and Gladiator.
explanation.definitionFit: The English film star, a famous hellraiser who died in 1999, is a performer of a past era.

clue.text: Butcher losing temper initially disturbed angelic child

indicators.note: disturbed means the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
losing tells us a letter is dropped from the butcher's word
initially picks out the opening letter of the word temper

explanation.surface: A butcher loses his temper and upsets a sweet little child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing temper initially' removes T from BUTCHER, leaving BUCHER; 'disturbed' rearranges BUCHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a winged infant angel in art, hence any sweet, innocent-looking child.

clue.text: Ambassador with a lawyer and revolutionary — a source of bother?

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
DA is a District Attorney, a US lawyer
Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: An ambassador, a lawyer and a revolutionary together sound like trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain in the head, or figuratively a nagging problem, is a cause of worry.

clue.text: Very hungry lad goes back round university after party

indicators.note: after places this piece behind the party word

parts.note: a rave is a lively party

indicators.note: round means the reversed word goes around the university letter
goes back means the word for lad is read in reverse

parts.note: a son is a lad

explanation.surface: A starving young man returns to campus after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes back' gives NOS, which 'round' wraps about the university letter; 'lad' is a son, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenous means voraciously hungry, like a ravening beast.

clue.text: Preclude three articles in fabric

parts.note: to bar is to prevent or preclude
a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article
a is the indefinite article again

explanation.surface: Ruling out three items of clothing made of a certain cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' means the grammar words A and THE, not items.
explanation.definitionFit: Barathea is a fine woollen cloth with a pebbled weave, used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: City director from France entering South Carolina is elated

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London, the financial district

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: SC is the US postal abbreviation for South Carolina
Jacques Tati was a French film director (Monsieur Hulot's Holiday)

explanation.surface: A French film director arrives in South Carolina and is delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' with a capital C is the City of London, London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in ecstasy is being overjoyed, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Hesitate, we hear, to make a statement of surrender

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for hesitate is said aloud, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: to waver is to hesitate or be undecided

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates, apparently, before formally giving up.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal document by which a right or claim is formally given up is a written relinquishment.

clue.text: Uninitiated soldiers interrupt movement of silent guard

indicators.note: interrupt means these letters break into the middle of the other piece
movement of the word silent means its letters are shifted about
uninitiated means without the first letter, so the word for soldiers loses its head

parts.note: men are soldiers, as in 'officers and men'

explanation.surface: Raw recruits disrupt the movements of a silent sentry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uninitiated' leaves EN; 'movement of' rearranges silent to S...TINEL, which EN interrupts after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a soldier posted on watch, a sentry or lookout.

clue.text: Tree tough to be seen after introduction of backward rule

indicators.text: to be seen after introduction of
indicators.note: to be seen after introduction of places the tough piece after the opening piece
backward means the word for rule is read from right to left

parts.note: a law is a rule
a tough is a hard man, a 'tough nut'

explanation.surface: A tough guy turns up after a backward rule is introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough' is a noun here, a hard man, rather than an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The walnut is a deciduous tree bearing edible wrinkled nuts and prized timber.

clue.text: Balance provided by label in the main this month

indicators.note: in means the label goes inside the other word

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the sea
a tag is a label
inst, short for instant, means this month in old business letters

explanation.surface: Making an adjustment, approved by labelling things at sea this month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic name for the open sea; 'inst.' is old commercial shorthand for this month.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset one thing against another is to weigh them against each other so as to balance them.

clue.text: Complaint about first signs of economic experiment not helping where internal growth is expected?

indicators.note: about means the complaint word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a grouse is a grumble or complaint

indicators.note: first signs of takes the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: Grumbling that an economic experiment is failing to help the economy grow.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials E, E, N, H go inside GROUSE. The definition plays on plants growing inside a glasshouse, while the surface suggests economic growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass building for raising plants is where they grow indoors, protected from the weather.

clue.text: Candidate from eastern country restricted by past wrong

indicators.note: restricted by means the country is held inside the other letters
wrong means the letters of past are set out incorrectly

parts.note: Iran is a country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: A candidate from an Eastern nation, hampered by a murky past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' rearranges PAST as ASP...T, holding IRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is someone who aspires to a position, a hopeful candidate.

clue.text: Hear about small creature detaining one missing school

indicators.note: about means the court word goes round the other letters

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court

indicators.note: detaining means the creature holds the next piece inside

parts.note: a runt is the smallest animal of a litter
A is one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A judge hears about a tiny animal holding someone missing class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is a judge's job: to hear a case is to try it. The smallest of a litter is its runt.
explanation.definitionFit: Truantry is the act of staying away from lessons without leave, absence from class.

clue.text: Asian citizen, one with feature favoured in Foreign Office

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the other

parts.note: FO is the British Foreign Office
I is the Roman numeral one
a lip is a facial feature
in means favoured, popular

explanation.surface: An Asian national with a favoured feature works at the Foreign Office.
explanation.walkthrough: The Foreign Office is the British government department for foreign affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A national of the Philippines, a country in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Perhaps private cinema is rebuilt after endless wait

indicators.note: after means this piece comes second in the answer
endless means the last letter of the word for wait is cut off

parts.note: to wait at table is to serve

indicators.note: is rebuilt means the letters of cinema are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A private cinema gets rebuilt after an interminable wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that a private is only one example of the definition; 'is rebuilt' gives ICEMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A private is the lowest rank of soldier, one example of a member of the armed forces.

clue.text: Severe gastric trouble? Not entirely!

indicators.note: not entirely says only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A bad stomach upset, though not quite completely.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from 'gastric' into 'trouble'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stern or uncompromising, rigid in enforcing rules, is a harsh demand.

clue.text: Woman tackling firm in Italian port

indicators.note: tackling means the woman takes on the firm, holding it inside her name

parts.note: Anna is a woman's name
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A woman takes on a company in an Italian harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancona is a seaport on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Hardened general put up in filthy place

indicators.note: in means the reversed general goes inside the filthy place

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, any filthy place

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word for general is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general

explanation.surface: A hardened general is billeted in a squalid hovel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' suits a down clue, read upwards; the general is Robert E. Lee of the American Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely means hard as steel, unyielding and toughened.

clue.text: Type that's inclined to take some capital I control

indicators.note: take some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A typeface sloping sideways invites you to grab some capital letter I for control.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping printed letters are called italic, a type leaning to the right.

clue.text: Soldier keeping time close to sergeant, a strict disciplinarian

indicators.note: keeping means the soldier word holds the time letter inside it

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving with the navy

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word sergeant

explanation.surface: A soldier keeps time near a sergeant, who is a stickler for discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside MARINE to make MARTINE, then the last letter of 'sergeant' is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after a famously severe French drillmaster, the word means someone who insists on rigid obedience.

clue.text: Get a temperature and short sign of infection

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a taint is a trace of contamination or infection

explanation.surface: Someone develops a fever and a brief symptom of infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' trims TAINT to TAIN. The surface reads 'Get a temperature' as catching a fever; 'Get' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain something is to achieve or reach it, a synonym of obtain.

clue.text: What counteracts a diet not working?

indicators.note: not working, with working read as being worked over, means these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking what remedy offsets a diet that is failing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface splits as 'a diet not working', but 'working' is the anagram signal applied to 'a diet not'.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy that neutralises a poison is one that works against its effects.

clue.text: Attractive prey for an older bird?

definitions.text: Attractive prey for an older bird?

parts.words: Attractive prey for an older bird?
parts.note: bird is British slang for a woman, so the prey is a handsome young man sought by an older woman, not a small animal hunted by a raptor

explanation.surface: An ageing bird of prey spots a tempting meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is British slang for a woman; the clue reads as a hawk hunting but means an older woman's young lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A much younger male lover kept by an older woman is the slang meaning, a plaything of a man.

clue.text: Chiselled out art, say, with no sign of oils

definitions.text: Chiselled out art, say, with no sign of oils

indicators.note: chiselled means the letters are hacked about into a new shape
with no means that letter is removed from the word next to it
sign of means the first letter of the word oils

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Art chipped out of stone, with no hint of oil paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no sign of oils' strips O from OUT, leaving UT; 'Chiselled' rearranges UT, ART and SAY. The whole clue also describes sculpture, carved rather than painted.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculpted figures collectively make up statuary: art carved in stone, not painted in oils.
